text:
We added retries to checkout and customers started getting double-charged.

Same amount. Same timestamp. Two transaction IDs. The client timed out and sent the request again. Our server had no idea it was the same intent.

Different week: SQS redelivered a signup message. Two welcome emails. Same root cause — we built for "happens once" in a world where the network guarantees at-least-once.

Fixes that actually work:

• Idempotency keys — client sends one key per checkout; server stores the result and replays it on duplicate
• Dedup by message/event ID on consumers
• Outbox pattern — DB write and "publish this event" in one transaction, relay retries safely

"Exactly-once" in production usually means at-least-once delivery plus idempotent handlers. Ask where dedup lives before you trust the label.
